title: Google Health app 5.12 update revamps glucose, blood pressure, and resilience tracking
summary: Google is releasing a big update for the Health app.
body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Version 5.12 of the Google Health app is rolling out. This version includes updates for medical records, health tracking, pregnancy tracking, nutrition, resilience, and Health Coach. The rollout is expected to continue over the next week in phases. Since the big rebrand, the Google Health experience has continued to be refined. Last month, the app received a fairly substantial update, adding new Health Guardian features for the Fitbit Air, improved sleep tracking, and more. This month, the update is just as large, with several updates ranging from health tracking to nutrition. Google has started the rollout of version 5.12 of the Health app. Although the rollout is starting today, it may take some time to hit your device. The company states that the update will have a phased release that will continue over the next week. This update is for both the Android and iOS versions of the app.

title: Gentle Monster teases Samsung Android XR glasses with some help from Joaquin Phoenix

body: TL;DR Pre-orders for Samsung’s Android XR glasses with frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster open next week, on November 12. Gentle Monster is sharing a teaser for a short film starring Joaquin Phoenix, designed to promote the launch. The full version will debut sometime around the middle of the month. Android XR smart glasses from Samsung are nearly here, with its Google-collab “Intelligent Eyewear” series featuring Warby Parker and Gentle Monster frames opening pre-orders next week — and ahead of that happening, we’re getting an early peek at how one of those companies is planning to hype up the launch. With all those big names involved, this one’s been shaping up to potentially be one of those product introductions that helps get the public really considering a new form factor. Google already took a shot at eyewear ages ago with Glass, and has long been living down the backlash. But now modern smart glasses are starting to build new momentum, and even in the face of renewed public criticism, we’re excited to see what these companies can do.

title: Samsung Health bug leaves users with missing step history
summary: Don't worry, you step data hasn't been wiped clean.
body: TL;DR Samsung Health users report that step counts recorded before November 2 have disappeared from the app’s Steps section following a recent update. The missing records remain accessible through Daily Activity, suggesting the data hasn’t been permanently deleted. Some users suspect a connection to the end of daylight saving time, but the cause remains unconfirmed. Updates are supposed to make apps better, whether that’s by introducing new features, refreshing the UI, or improving performance, but it’s a different story when those very updates end up breaking functionality that worked perfectly fine before — yet that’s seemingly what some Samsung Health users are experiencing right now. Several Samsung Health users are reporting that their historical step counts have disappeared from the app. Most of the affected users say this happened after the November 2nd Samsung Health update. More specifically, those users say step counts recorded prior to November 2nd aren’t showing up in the app’s Steps section. Checking the same dates on the app’s Daily Activity section still highlights the step counts.

title: فيديو: ياسر القحطاني يكشف.. لماذا عبدالله الحمدان أفضل في النصر من الهلال؟
summary: سؤال مثير للجدل حول المهاجم السعودي
body: سؤال مثير للجدل حول المهاجم السعودي كشف ياسر القحطاني، نجم الكرة السعودية، عن سبب تألق عبدالله الحمدان، مهاجم النصر، رفقة "العالمي"، وتفوقه على ما كان يقدمه مع ناديه السابق الهلال. وقال عبدالله العنزي، حارس النصر السابق، في تصريحات لقنوات "ثمانية": "أرى أن عبدالله الحمدان وجد نفسه في النصر أكثر من أي نادٍ آخر، ليس تقليلًا، ولكن ربما عامل الخبرة وكثرة المشاركات والمجموعة". ورد القحطاني: "ربما يكون الأمر بسبب ثقة المدرب فيه بشكل أكبر، ومنحه عددًا أكبر من المشاركات، وكذلك الجمهور الذي منحه الثقة والدعم". وأضاف: "الفارق أيضًا أنه ثابت في مركزه مع النصر، أما في الهلال، فقد تنقل من مركز إلى مركز حتى تاه في الملعب". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة غير أن مناف أبو شقير، نجم الاتحاد السابق، اعترض على تلك الفكرة، قائلًا: "من المباريات التي أعجبني فيها الحمدان مباراة المنتخب (السعودي) مع الصين، والتي لعب فيها كجناح أيسر". وأتم: "صحيح أنه وجد مكانه في النصر، لكن لا يزال من الممكن توظيفه على الطرف، كما يحدث مع فراس البريكان لاعب الأهلي، وكما كان يحدث مع ياسر القحطاني نفسه". عبدالله العنزي @22Alenizi 🎙️ «عبدالله الحمدان لقى نفسه في النصر أكثر من أي نادٍ آخر، مو تقليل، ولكن بعض الأوقات ممكن عامل الخبرة مع مرور الوقت، وممكن تكون المجموعة أو كثرة المشاركات أتاحت له الفرصة.» نق…

title: Some Nest doorbells have stopped showing the live video feed
summary: Can’t see who’s at the door? You aren't the only one.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Nest doorbell owners are reporting that live view has stopped working. The issue appears to be mostly affecting the Nest Hello doorbell. One of the reasons to buy a Nest doorbell is for its camera. With this camera, you can monitor, record, and interact with activity at your front door. Of course, a key component to all of this is the doorbell’s live video feed. However, an issue is now interfering with this feature. If you’ve been having trouble with the Live View feature on your Nest doorbell, you’re not alone. Users are flocking to Reddit to report that Live View is broken. For some, it appears the issue popped up about a week ago. However, others have been dealing with the bug for longer than that.

title: Google’s November Pixel update is missing, and Android 17 QPR2 may explain why
summary: November's missing update has sparked an intriguing theory.
body: TL;DR November Pixel update hasn’t arrived, breaking the first-Tuesday release pattern that Google has followed for most monthly updates this year. Android security database entries and reported release candidate builds suggest Android 17 QPR2 could arrive earlier than its expected December release. Google hasn’t confirmed an early QPR2 rollout or explained the November update’s absence. Google’s Pixel update calendar has been quite predictable this year, until November apparently went off-script. Regular security patches have generally landed on the first Tuesday of the month, while bigger Android releases have taken a little longer. But November’s first Tuesday has come and gone without an update, raising an interesting question: Is Google preparing something bigger than the usual security fixes? A Reddit user believes the answer could be Android 17 QPR2, which has generally been expected in December.

A fresh update is finally arriving, but it isn’t the one they’ve been waiting for. title: How I freed up 4GB of storage to avoid paying for Google One
summary: I cleared enough clutter to avoid paying for another monthly subscription.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I’ve been cruising in Google’s free storage tier for as long as I can remember, backing up my Photos, emails, and even WhatsApp messages without ever spending a penny. But over the past few months, I’ve been creeping up to the 15GB cap (17GB in my case , as an old-timer who jumped through Google’s security hoops), leading to a barrage of Google One notifications urging me to upgrade to a paid storage tier. That’s never going to happen. The economics of starting out at just $1.99 a month for 100GB might not sound like much, but I know it won’t be many more years before I hit that limit, too. Then I’d be hooked: forking out $4.99 and then $9.99 every month, in perpetuity, for the luxury of having Google back up my odds and ends. Granted, Google One might be worth the cost if you want Gemini in your docs and double AI usage without forking out for yet another monthly plan. But for me, I’m happy just using the free allowance to keep the most recent things I need within quick reach. I could store everything else on a USB stick or external hard drive for cheap.

body: Credit: Aina TL;DR Aina is a smart ring with a screen and a button. The bigger attraction is its context-aware cues, which interact with your phone and PC to control them or interact with your AI agents. The onboard AI is claimed to predict your next steps and take action automatically, such as ordering an Uber only after you finish breakfast. It’s available for pre-ordering and will start shipping early next year. Smart rings have lately been seen as viable alternatives to smartwatches because of their non-existent footprint, which makes them easier to wear all day. However, smart rings lack the interactive features of a smartwatch , or other abilities that make them an extension of your smartphone, not just another accessory. title: I love big Si-C batteries, but slow charging is a steep price to pay
summary: Bigger batteries sound great, but are slower charging speeds worth the extra capacity?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority If there’s been one major game changer for smartphone hardware in the past few years, it’s undoubtedly the adoption of silicon-carbon (Si-C) battery technology. By mixing traditional lithium-ion cells with silicon-carbon, manufacturers are able to greatly increase a battery’s storage capacity without a huge increase in its physical size, meaning better longevity for our smartphones. Even small amounts of added Si-C have been a game changer for battery capacities. After being stuck with 5,000mAh Li-ion cells as the upper limit for the best part of a decade, we’ve quickly seen capacities jump to 7,000mAh, 8,000mAh, and even 10,000mAh cells in the most advanced cases.

title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
summary: Android sabotages itself next.
body: TL;DR Bitdefender researchers discovered an Android vulnerability that can trigger an endless crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted APK, potentially leaving devices unusable. The flaw exploits how Android handles ZIP compression methods, repeatedly crashing the core system_server process. Recovering may require a factory reset or manually deleting the malicious file using ADB. No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses. We recently shared information about malware that can empty your bank accounts in secret , and now, researchers have found a separate Android flaw that could leave your phone outright unusable. Normally, malicious apps need to request permissions and execute code to attack your device. However, researchers at Bitdefender have discovered a new vulnerability dubbed GhostMap that triggers a crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted app.

We’ve seen Nintendo Switch 2 emulators landing on various platforms in the last week or two, and they all seem to be ultimately based on the acclaimed Eden emulator for Nintendo Switch 1 titles. Android isn’t left out of the fun, as we’ve also seen Eden SX2A , which is based on the PokeDinner emulator for other platforms. In fact, PokeDinner is in turn based on the so-called Eglantine emulator. And that particular emulator is based on Eden-NS2, which is itself a fork of the original Eden emulator for Nintendo Switch 1 titles. Forking heck.

body: TL;DR Several Samsung users have reported issues with mobile data, Wi-Fi, and SIM detection after updating to One UI 9. Restarting the phone or toggling airplane mode seems to temporarily resolve the problem. A permanent fix hasn’t been discovered for any of the connectivity problems. Samsung has been rolling out the stable One UI 9 update to Galaxy phones over the last few months. Although it introduces several new features and brings some Galaxy AI features to older Samsung flagships, the update process doesn’t seem to be going smoothly for everyone. According to threads on Reddit and the Samsung Community forums , several users have been experiencing connectivity problems since installing the One UI 9 update. The problems range from Wi-Fi and cellular data issues to phones failing to detect SIM cards.

Long-pressing a conversation will soon pop up recent messages and a refreshed context menu, while leaving the sender’s message unread. Unlike iOS, Android’s peekable preview card will let you scroll up to inspect more messages discreetly. WhatsApp offers users a global toggle for read receipts, letting them control whether they send and receive blue ticks for when messages are read. Many people keep read receipts off entirely, while others keep them on. Those in the second camp often find themselves wanting to know more about a message without sending a read receipt (two blue ticks). You can glean information from the message notification, but this doesn’t work out if you’ve already swiped away the notification or you get too many messages to keep track of. iOS users have long had a way to peek at messages without triggering a read receipt, and we’ve now spotted clues that this could be coming to WhatsApp on Android too. title: Xbox Cloud Gaming now lets your phone double as a controller on smart TVs
summary: No controller? No problem.
body: TL;DR A new Xbox Cloud Gaming preview lets you use your phone as a controller on supported smart TVs. It works with Android and iOS devices, and you don’t even need to download an app. Xbox is also previewing cloud connect for the Xbox Nano Controller in the US. Cloud connect lets the Xbox Nano Controller connect directly to cloud servers over Wi-Fi, which Microsoft says can help reduce input lag. Xbox Cloud Gaming is a convenient way to play Xbox games on your smart TV without a console. But what if you don’t have a controller handy? Microsoft is now trying to fix that by letting you turn your phone into an Xbox controller. The company has announced two new Xbox Cloud Gaming previews. The first lets you use an Android or iOS phone as a makeshift controller on supported smart TVs. You connect by scanning a QR code on your TV, and the controls open in your phone’s browser, meaning you don’t even need to download an app. What’s more, some games will feature control layouts tailored to how they play.

The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn’s 500 kilometer diameter moon . Discovered by Cassini in 2005, the icy plumes are likely connected to an ocean beneath the ice shell of Enceladus. They supply material directly to Saturn’s outer, tenuous E ring and make the surface of Enceladus as reflective as snow. Across the scene, Saturn’s icy rings scatter sunlight toward Cassini’s cameras. Beyond the rings (lower right), the night side of 80 kilometer diameter moon Pandora is faintly lit by Saturnlight .
